key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within hours to 1-2 days. Often triggered by ALCOHOL BINGE or HEAVY FATTY MEAL (gallstones). LOCATION: Epigastric (upper mid-abdomen) and periumbilical. RADIATES STRAIGHT THROUGH TO THE BACK in 'boring' or 'band-like' pattern - highly characteristic. May radiate to left upper quadrant. DURATION: CONSTANT pain lasting hours to days (not episodic). CHARACTER: DEEP ACHING or KNIFE-LIKE. Described as boring, penetrating, or band-like across upper abdomen. AGGRAVATING: WORSE WHEN LYING FLAT. Pain intensifies in supine position. RELIEVING: BETTER WHEN SITTING UP AND LEANING FORWARD. Patients assume 'fetal position' or lean forward for relief. TIMING: CONSTANT and unrelenting. Persists continuously (not waves). SEVERITY: 8-10/10, very severe and debilitating. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: PERSISTENT NAUSEA AND VOMITING (severe, not relieved by vomiting), anorexia, low-grade fever, abdominal distension. KEY POSITIVES: Epigastric→back radiation, relief with leaning forward, alcohol/fatty meal trigger, persistent vomiting. KEY NEGATIVES: Pain NOT radiating to back is atypical. Diarrhea uncommon initially. right lower quadrant (RLQ) pain suggests appendicitis not pancreatitis.

red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with hypotension or tachycardia - severe pancreatitis with third-spacing, needs ICU
Respiratory distress or low oxygen saturation - ARDS complication, call 911
Altered mental status, severe dehydration - severe systemic inflammation
Grey-Turner sign (flank bruising) or Cullen sign (periumbilical bruising) - hemorrhagic pancreatitis, very severe
